big-news.text: Innovasjon Norge (Innovation Norway) bought ad space on Times Square in New York, and the screens take a cheeky swipe at Trump's insults about Norway.
Kongsseteren, the royal family's private mountain lodge at Voksenkollen, has changed hands after King Harald's death, and people are guessing who will live there now.
A new poll says most Ap (Labour) voters want to leave Arctic oil in the ground, but the Ap government wants the Wisting field developed.
Rosenborg's Amin Chiakha, the top scorer in Eliteserien (Norway's top football league), scored twice in a 3–0 win in Fredrikstad but left upset. The referee confirms there are accusations of racism.

whats-changing.text: Starting today, the cheaper 495 kr monthly pass for zone 1 is live. Single tickets stay at 46 kr.

oslo.text: Up to 1,000 people protested at Regjeringskvartalet, the government quarter, on Saturday against a planned explosives factory in Hurum.
A man died after an accident at the Sats gym at CC Vest on Saturday, and the police are investigating.

be-aware.text: Police in Oslo and Bærum say autopsy findings point to a sharp object, which makes them more suspicious that a person is behind a string of cat deaths.
There are no weather warnings for Oslo. It's mild today at around 8 to 10°C and will cool to about 2 to 5°C by Friday.

fun-and-free.text: Top pick: The Frank Znort Quartet plays a free show at Blå today at 16:30, and the Birkelunden market is open from 12:00 if you want to browse first.
Chamber Music Week runs Nov 2 to 7 at the Norwegian Academy of Music, and every concert is free except Friday's chamber orchestra.
Oslo Zine Fest is free on Nov 7 and 8 at ROM for kunst og arkitektur, with a zine market from 12:00 to 17:00 plus workshops.
Fjord Oslo starts Thursday, Nov 5, and this year's theme is "Imagine Peace".
